parties:
Bulbul Begum ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md Sanwar Belal and anr ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: The present appeal, by leave, is by the plaintiff against the judgment and order dated December, 2 1997 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1056 of 1995 making the Rule absolute and thereby dismissing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated November 26, 1994 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Sadar, Chittagong in Small Cause Court Suit No. 3 of 1989. Plaintiff filed the said suit seeking eviction of the monthly tenant on the ground of default in the payment of rent as well as on the ground of bonafide requirement of the premises for her own use and occupation upon construction of a modern residential house. 

 2. Plaintiffs case, inter alia, is that she has become the owner of the premises in suit on the basis of gift made by her mother and the defendants are occupying the premises in suit as tenant at the rent of Taka 400 per month payable according to English Calendar by the 15th of the next month; that defendant No. 1 is the managing partner of the defendant No. 2, which is a registered partnership firm; that the tenant was paying rent through money order irregularly, that defendants did not pay the rent of May, 1988 within the specified time consequent thereupon being a defaulter has made them liable to be evicted. It is the further case of the plaintiff that she requires the suit premises for construction of modern residential building for her own use and occupation since she or her husband has no house in Chittagong or Dhaka or anywhere else except the paternal joint family house of her husband in Chittagong; that she served notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating the tenancy and requesting the defendants to vacate the suit premises by December 31, 1988 but they did not pay any heed to her request and that they are in occupation of the suit premises unauthorized. The plaintiff claimed compensation @ Taka 50 per day from 1st January, 1989 to February 26, 1989. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that defendant No. 1's father late Abdul Motaleb took lease of the suit premises from the mother of the plaintiff on the basis of an agreement of June 15, 1955 at a rental of Taka 80 per month and he established a proprietary Engineering Workshop, Ambia Engineering Workshop, and carried on his business. After expiry of the initial lease term another lease agreement dated June 10, 1957 was entered into and the rent was enhanced to Taka 100, that defendant No. is father on obtaining permission from the landlady, i.e. plaintiffs mother, constructed but spending Taka 2,000 and although landlady promised to pay the said amount but did not pay the same; that in 1958 there was fire and the structures in the suit premises were burnt into ashes and thereupon defendant No. is father made construction in the suit premises with the permission of the landlady by spending Taka 4,200; that there was an oral agreement between the landlady and defendant No. 1's father that the money so spent would be deducted @ Taka 50 per month from the rent, that during subsistence of the tenancy at one stage landlady refused to accept rent and thereupon defendant No. is father deposited rent in the Court and that after prolonged litigations finally the landlady accepted rent from defendant No. 1's father and by mutual agreement rent was enhanced to Taka 200 per month and the landlady accepted the rent at that rate up to March 1979 and thereupon from the month of April refused to accept the rent and then defendant No. 1's father deposited the rent in Court by filing Rent Deposit Case No. 338 of 1979 and the said case was disposed of on May 18, 1982 and the landlady accepted rent thereafter, that defendant No. 1's father died on October 15, 1982 leaving sons and daughters as well as a wife and although they are the tenants of the suit premises but no notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served upon all of them and they have also not been made parties in the suit. It is also the contention of the defendants that the notice so served is neither proper nor sufficient and the claim of bonafide requirement is not genuine and also baseless since the suit premises is a commercial plot within commercial area and the question of construction of a residential building is a malafide plea taken for evicting them. 

 4. The trial Court on detailed discussions and consideration of the evidence of the parties decreed the suit upon arriving at the findings that the notice served under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 is quite in accordance with law and also sufficient and the same was duly served on the defendants; that the defendants have defaulted in the payment of rent for the month of May, 1988 within the specified time i.e. within June 15, 1988, as such, they are defaulters and the plaintiff bonafide requires the premises for her own use and occupation upon constructing a residential building, that the defendants are the tenants of the suit premises and that defendant No. 1's father did not take lease of the vacant land and the tenant did not construct any house in the guilt premises; that the suit is not bad for defect of party; that the plaintiff is entitled to compensation at a rate Taka 25 per day from 1st of June, 1989 till vacating of the premises in suit. 

 5. As against the judgment and decree of the Small Cause Court the defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissed the suit on the findings that the SCC Suit is bad for defect of party since after death of Abdul Motaleb his sons, daughters and wife have become tenants of the premises in suit but the suit has been filed impleading one of the sons and the firm Ambia Engineering Workshop which was and is never a tenant, but Abdul Motaleb the proprietor of the said firm was the tenant and, as such, the suit so filed is not maintainable as the decree passed in the suit is not binding upon the other heirs of Abdul Motaleb, that from the materials on record it is seen that "it was the practice of the plaintiff and her predecessor Rezia to realise rent in lump and because of that conduct the plaintiff waived the right to realise rent by the 15th of next month-----------But the Court below without considering this plea of waiver held the defendant to be defaulter by one day for the month of May, 1988 on 16th June, 1988. This finding of the court below suffers from total non-consideration of the series of rent receipts and evidence on record showing the mode of payment of rent making out a case of waiver". 

 7. Leave has been granted to consider the submission whether the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was properly and legally served on the Managing Partner of the registered partnership and the Firm and whether there was any defect as regards service of notice, whether the defendants are defaulters in the payment of rent as per agreement, whether receiving of rent in lump for several months by the landlady does constitute waiver and acquiescence varying the terms of written agreement exempting the tenant from the liability of payment of rent as per agreement or in the absence of a written agreement within the time specified in the statute, whether the High Court Division was in error in not holding that the plaintiff has bonafide requirement of the suit premises to construct a residential house as she has no other premises either in Dhaka or in Chittagong, whether the High Court Division was correct in holding that the suit was bad for defect of parties for non-impleading the heirs of original tenant Abdul Motalib when defendant No. 1 in his deposition has stated that he is Managing Partner of the defendant No. 2, a firm registered in the office of the Registrar of Firms. 

 10. Now let us turn to the question of waiver of the term of payment of rent by the 15th of the next month. The High Court Division in the background of payment of rent of more than one month at a time by the tenant and accepting thereof by the landlady for some time was of the view that there was waiver on the part of landlady regards payment of rent within the agreed period or by the 15th of the next month and thereupon held that the tenant was not a defaulter. Plaintiff's case is that as per term of agreement the tenant was required to pay the rent due for the month by the 15th of the next month. It is in the evidence of PW 1 that plaintiff accepted the rent that defendant used to send for more than one month at a time by Money Order and although she accepted the same but that was not the regular practice. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that defendant paid the rent for the month of June and July, 1972 in August 1972, rent for the month of August and September, 1972 in October 1972, rent for the month of October, November and December, 1972 in January 1973, rent for the month of January and February, 1973 in March 1973, rent for the month of March, April and May, 1973 in May 1973, rent for the month of October, November and December, 1973 in January 1974, rent for the month of May and June, 1974 in July 1974, rent for the month of July, August and September, 1974 in October, 1974 and rent for the month of October end November, 1974 in the month of December, 1974, rent for the month of December, 1974 and January, 1975 in February, 1975, rent for the month of February, March and April, 1985 in May, 1985. The rent was paid either obtaining rent receipt or by Money Order. From the material on record it is seen it was not the usual or regular practice on the part of the landlady to accept rent in lump, rather of intermittent occasions tenant paid the rents for more than one month at a time and the landlady accepted the same. There is total absence of evidence since May, 1985 till April, 1988 the tenant on any occasion paid rent in lump and the same was accepted by the landlady. The learned Advocate for the respondent upon referring to the materials on record could not point out that the tenant at any point of time paid rent in lump or more than one month at a time since May 1985 to April, 1988 and the landlady accepted the same. The High Court Division upon referring to intermittent payment of rent of two or three months at a time in the year, 1972 to 1975 and then in the first quarter of 1985 (Exhibits 'Gha' 59 to 70 and Exhibits 'Gha' 13 to 32), but overlooking the fact that since May, 1985 there was no payment of rent either in lump for several months or more than one month at a time reversed the finding of the trial Court accepting defendant's contention of waiver by plaintiff of the terms of contract relating to payment of rent of the month fallen due by the 15th of the next month. The defendant in support of his case of waiver by the plaintiff of the contract for payment of rent by the 15th of the next month since May 1985 till May, 1988 has not produced any evidence. The defendant was required to establish his case of waiver as to contract of payment of rent by evidence (40 DLR (AD) 1). The law is also settled now that irregular payment of rent for several months at a time, in the absence of written contract or understanding with the landlord would not constitute waiver of the right to receive rent as per provision of section 18(5) of the Premises' Rent Control Act, 1991 (1984 BLD (AD) 298 and 33 DLR (AD) 55). In that view of the matter the High Court Division was in error in holding that the plaintiff waived his right of receiving the rent by the 15th of the next month and consequently was in error in holding defendant was not a defaulter for non-payment of the rent of May, 1988 by the 15th of the next month i.e. by June 15, 1988. The moot point is, whether defendant is a defaulter for not paying the rent of the month of May, 1988 by June 15, 1988. It is not disputed that as per agreement tenant was required to pay rent of the month became due by the 15th of the next month. Plaintiff has filed the suit upon making the averment that defendant did not pay the rent of May, 1988 within June 15, 1988. In support of the said averment she has examined PW 1 and filed Exhibit 6. The exhibit 6 has been put into evidence to establish that rent for the month of May, 1988 was sent on June 16, 1988 by money order and the same was received by the plaintiff on June 28, 1988. The defendant tried to dislodge Exhibit 6 upon asserting that he sent the rent of the month of May, 1988 within the agreed time, but to substantiate the said assertion did not submit the receipt issued by the postal department while receiving the Money Order addressed to the defendant's landlady, on the contrary has submitted the receipt which was delivered to him by the postal department after making payment of the money sent by money order and this receipt has been marked as Exhibit 13 and the same shows that the Money Order was delivered to the plaintiff on June 28, 1988. The trial Court upon consideration of these 2 Exhibits i.e. Exhibit 6 and Exhibit "Gha 13" arrived at the finding that rent for the month of May, 1988 was sent after June 15, 1988 and thereby the tenant defaulted in the payment of rent within the specified time. The High Court Division has set aside the finding of the trial Court relating to the question of tenant's being defaulter upon observing "Exhibit 6 does not show who was the sender of the money order and on what account the money was paid". Plaintiff's witness PW 1 has stated that plaintiff ascertained from the GPO that defendant sent rent of May, 1988 by the Money Order dated 16-6-1988 and that the money order was paid to the plaintiff on 28-6-1988 and on her asking the postal authority issued the Exhibit 6. It may be mentioned although defendant claimed that rent for the month of May, 1988 was paid within June 15, 1988 but in support thereof as mentioned earlier he has not produced any documentary evidence, although the receipt issued by the Postal Department while receiving the Money Order was very much with him but has submitted the Money Order receipt (Exhibit 13) showing payment of the amount of the Money Order to the addressee on 28-6-1988. Plaintiff discharged her burden of establishing the fact that defendant sent the rent for the month of May, 1988 after June 15, 1988. It was a requirement for the defendant to disprove the said fact, but he did not take any step to disprove the oral as well as documentary evidence produced from the side of the plaintiff in assertion of the fact that rent for the month of May, 1988 was sent by Money Order after June 15, 1988. In the afore state of the matter the High Court Division was in error in holding that defendant was not a defaulter in the payment of rent for the month of May, 1988 within the specified time. The law requires the tenant to pay the rent of the month became due either by the date as per terms of contract or by the 15th of the next month and default thereof visits him with the consequence as provided in law. (41 DLR (AD) 88, 31 DLR (AD) 183). 

 11. There now remains the question of bonafide requirement of the premises in suit by the plaintiff for her own use and occupation upon constructing the residential house. The claim of the plaintiff is that she requires the premises in suit for her own use and occupation upon construction of a residential house was opposed by the defendant contending that plaintiff has got property from her parents and she has other property in Chittagong town and that plaintiff's husband has paternal homestead in North Kattali, Chittagong. It was also contended by the defendants that the premises in question is in a commercial area and since 1955 defendant No. 1's father and after the death of his father defendant No. 1 and his brothers, sisters and mother were carrying on business in the suit premises and, as such, there arises no question of construction of a residential house in the suit premises for use and occupation of the plaintiff. 

 14. The learned Advocate for the respondent in supporting the judgment of the High Court Division as regards the question of absence of bonafide requirement by the plaintiff of the premises in suit because of the location of the suit premises and in support of the contention as to absence of element of muse relating to requirement of the premises has referred to the case reported in 5 MLR (AD), 295 and PLD 2000 (SC) 829. Suffice it to say in the background of the unrebutted fact it can reasonably be said that the plaintiff has very much been able to make out a case of bonafide requirement of the premises in suit showing presence of element of 'must'. The plaintiff has shown that she has no other premises either in Chittagong or in Dhaka except the premises in suit and that she needs the same for her own use and occupation upon constructing a residential house. In that state of the matter genuinely element of 'must' is present relating to bonafide requirement of the premises by the plaintiff and, as such, the case referred to reported in 5 MLR (AD) 295 is of no help to the respondent. In the case reported in PLD 2000 (SC) 829 it has been held amongst others "It may be noted that as far as the requirement of rented land for personal bonafide use is concerned, it ought to be proved as a fact through cogent, convincing and trustworthy evidence. Mere a desire of the landlord that he intends to occupy a particular premises, may be residential or non-residential or rented land, itself would not be sufficient to accept his claim unless the requirement/need is proved as a matter of fact "It has already been observed by us that plaintiff by reliable evidence has established her case of bonafide requirement of the premises for her own use and occupation upon constructing a residential house.
